items.headline: Islandwide framework to defuse neighbour disputes and noise from Sept 1
items.summary: From Sept 1, HDB and the People's Association can issue binding Mediation Directions in public-housing estates, with the People's Association covering private estates, and an expanded Community Relations Unit will step in on severe noise cases. The rollout follows a pilot and aims to settle disputes before they escalate to the courts.

items.headline: About 1.5 million Singaporeans to receive up to S$850 in GST Voucher cash this month
items.summary: Around 1.5 million adult Singaporeans are getting up to S$850 in cash under the August GST Voucher payout, with eligibility tied to a 2025 assessable income of up to S$39,000 and owning no more than one property. About 710,000 seniors also receive up to S$450 in MediSave top-ups.

items.headline: BTO income ceiling raised to S$16,000, with more ballot chances for families
items.summary: The household income ceiling to buy a new Build-To-Order flat rises from S$14,000 to S$16,000, and families with children get additional ballot chances. The changes are part of a housing package unveiled around this year's National Day Rally.

items.headline: Government studying a lower age for singles to buy HDB flats
items.summary: National Development Minister Chee Hong Tat said the government is considering lowering the eligibility age for singles to buy HDB flats below the current 35. Any change would be phased in to manage demand.

items.headline: India's foreign-exchange reserves hit a record $729 billion
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India's reserves rose $12.4 billion to an all-time high of about $729.3 billion in the week to Aug 21, surpassing the previous February peak, as the central bank steps up efforts to steady the rupee. The rupee has still weakened more than 8% over the past year.

items.headline: India's top-rated firms borrow long as bets on RBI rate hikes grow
items.summary: Some of India's highest-rated companies, including Power Finance Corp. and its unit REC, are pulling shorter-tenor bond sales and pricing 10- to 15-year issues instead, as investors wager the RBI's next move is up. For top borrowers, longer debt has become relatively cheaper than three-year paper.

items.headline: RBI shifts to steady intervention to defend the rupee
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has moved to a more constant pattern of market intervention, stepping in whenever the rupee weakens rather than only to curb large swings, aided by strong foreign-deposit inflows. The rupee traded near 95.5 to the dollar.

items.headline: UK economy hands Burnham an early boost before his first budget
items.summary: Britain's services sector posted its best growth in six months and consumer confidence hit a two-year high, an early lift for Prime Minister Andy Burnham ahead of his first autumn budget. Economists caution that inflation looks set to push past 3% and public borrowing is running above forecast.

items.headline: Ukraine reinforces the Donetsk front to choke Russia's weapons supply
items.summary: Ukraine is reinforcing positions around Donetsk and striking Russian logistics as it tries to disrupt the flow of weapons to the front line, even as both sides trade drone and missile attacks. Kyiv's European allies are weighing how to close a looming air-defence gap.

items.headline: Qatar's PM visits Tehran to revive US-Iran talks amid a sanctions push
items.summary: Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani met Iran's foreign minister in Tehran to try to revive diplomacy after Washington vowed to intensify economic pressure on Tehran. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's campaign targets more than 60 entities across digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping.

items.headline: US envoy warns a collapse of the Gaza truce would be a point of no return
items.summary: The lead US official for Gaza warned that a failure of the fragile ceasefire process would mark a point of no return, as negotiations stall over disarmament and an Israeli withdrawal. The truce has held unevenly since a US-backed plan took effect.

items.headline: Six months on, the US-Israel war on Iran settles into a stalemate
items.summary: Al Jazeera tallied the toll six months after the US and Israel launched strikes on Iran, a conflict that has drawn in Hezbollah and repeated Israeli responses and left the region in a grinding standoff. Iran continues to use its leverage over the Strait of Hormuz to pressure Washington and global energy markets.

items.headline: Update: Nvidia agrees to buy Hugging Face for about $12.9 billion
items.summary: Nvidia has reached an agreement to acquire Hugging Face, the widely used platform for sharing open-source AI models, in a deal valuing it at roughly $12.9 billion. The price is nearly triple the $4.5 billion valuation Hugging Face carried in 2023, when Nvidia was among its investors.

items.headline: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and 100-plus firms urge a surge in cyber defence
items.summary: More than 100 technology and security companies, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Cloudflare and CrowdStrike, signed an open letter warning that AI-enabled cyberattacks will grow far more widespread and sophisticated in the coming months. They called for a global surge in cyber defence and expanded protection for hospitals, utilities and local governments.

items.headline: OpenAI starts showing ads on ChatGPT in India
items.summary: OpenAI began serving ads to users on ChatGPT's free tier and its 399-rupee Go plan in India, launching with 50 brands and agency partners WPP and Omnicom as it builds revenue ahead of a planned 2027 IPO. A self-serve ad manager opens on Sept 4 with a daily minimum budget of about 725 rupees.

items.headline: Consumer-AI startup Instinct raises $350 million at a $2.5 billion valuation
items.summary: Instinct, a consumer AI assistant still in private beta, raised $350 million at a $2.5 billion valuation, a sign that investors remain willing to place large early bets on products that could become new consumer interfaces. The round underscores continued appetite for consumer-facing AI.

items.headline: Apple sets a Sept 9 event for its first foldable iPhone
items.summary: Apple will hold its biggest launch of the year on Sept 9, where it is expected to unveil the iPhone 18 Pro line and a foldable iPhone reported to be branded the iPhone Ultra, with a starting price at or above $2,000. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman says the event also opens the tenure of new chief executive John Ternus.

items.headline: Fed's Warsh warns inflation is too high, lifting bets on a September rate hike
items.summary: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh told the Jackson Hole symposium that inflation remains above the 2% target and that this summer's better readings do not signal a lasting improvement, pushing market odds of a September rate hike above 50%. The S&P 500 slipped 0.25% to 7,711.76 on Friday but still posted a winning week.

items.headline: Advent and Stripe abandon a $50 billion-plus pursuit of PayPal
items.summary: A consortium of buyout firm Advent International and payments company Stripe walked away from a potential acquisition of PayPal that would have topped $50 billion, ending one of the year's biggest buyout talks. PayPal shares tumbled as much as 16% after weeks of gains on takeover hopes.

items.headline: Marvell posts record revenue but shares slide on a cautious outlook
items.summary: Marvell Technology reported record fiscal second-quarter revenue of about $2.74 billion, up 37% from a year earlier, and lifted its full-year outlook to roughly 50% growth. The stock still fell about 6% as the raised guidance failed to meet lofty expectations and material revenue from its Google partnership was pushed to fiscal 2029.

items.headline: Judge blocks the Pentagon's blacklisting of Anthropic as unlawful
items.summary: US District Judge Rita Lin ruled that the Defense Department acted illegally in designating AI firm Anthropic a national-security supply-chain risk, calling it retaliation for the company's criticism of Pentagon AI policy and a violation of its First and Fifth Amendment rights. The decision restores Anthropic's access to military contracts the company said were worth potentially billions.

items.headline: India draw the Colombo Test as Dinusha defies them, but clinch the series 1-0
items.summary: Sonal Dinusha's defiant unbeaten 133 steered Sri Lanka to a draw in the second Test in Colombo, batting a combined 426 balls after India declared on 503-9. India still won the two-Test series 1-0.

items.headline: US Open begins Sunday with Alcaraz and Sabalenka defending, Sinner out injured
items.summary: The year's final Grand Slam starts Sunday at Flushing Meadows, with Carlos Alcaraz opening his title defence against Roman Safiullin and Aryna Sabalenka chasing a third straight women's crown. World No. 1 Jannik Sinner misses the tournament with a knee injury, lifting Alexander Zverev to the top seeding.

items.headline: Ferrari bring an upgraded engine to Monza as Antonelli takes a home grid penalty
items.summary: Ferrari will run upgraded power units for Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc at their home Italian Grand Prix without grid penalties, while championship leader Kimi Antonelli drops down the order after taking a fresh engine. Antonelli leads George Russell and Hamilton by 59 points, though Lando Norris, 83 back, has won the last two races.

items.headline: Hamilton set to extend at Ferrari as F1's driver market settles
items.summary: Lewis Hamilton is expected to confirm a new Ferrari contract around the Italian Grand Prix at Monza, after Max Verstappen's deal to 2030 and Carlos Sainz's Williams extension reshaped the grid. Reigning champion Lando Norris is reportedly in talks with McLaren over a package worth about $70 million a year.

items.headline: NASA's Roman Space Telescope is cleared for a Falcon Heavy launch
items.summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is go for launch after a readiness review, with liftoff set for Aug 30 on a SpaceX Falcon Heavy from Kennedy Space Center. From a perch a million miles out, Roman is designed to survey dark matter and dark energy and could uncover thousands of exoplanets.

items.headline: Scientists map a brain circuit that acts as a brake on chronic pain
items.summary: Researchers reported a spino-brain-spinal cord loop that drives chronic mechanical pain in mice, and found that silencing specific cells along it eliminates hypersensitivity while preserving normal, protective pain responses. The work, published in Nature, points to new targets for treating chronic pain without opioids.

items.headline: JWST finds hidden faint stars making early galaxies far more massive
items.summary: Deep James Webb spectra of nine early massive galaxies reveal far more small, low-mass stars than expected, a bottom-heavy mix that could make some galaxies up to four times more massive than measured. The result, published in Nature Astronomy, sharpens the tension between the early universe and galaxy-formation models.

items.headline: Europe's newest weather satellite reaches orbit on Ariane 6
items.summary: Arianespace launched the MTG-I2 imaging satellite, developed by ESA and EUMETSAT, on Ariane 6's first mission to geostationary transfer orbit from French Guiana. It completes the first family of the Meteosat Third Generation system and will deliver rapid-scan imagery over Europe every 2.5 minutes to sharpen severe-storm warnings.

fun_fact.headline: Scotland's national animal is the unicorn
fun_fact.body: Scotland's official national animal is the unicorn. The mythical beast has been a Scottish royal symbol since the 1400s, chosen as an emblem of purity, pride and untameable strength, and a chained unicorn still supports the United Kingdom's royal coat of arms today. The chain is said to signal the creature's ferocity - so wild that only a king could tame it.
fun_fact.source: National Records of Scotland; Historic Environment Scotland

puzzle.title: All Labels Are Wrong
puzzle.body: Three boxes hold apples only, oranges only, and a mix; all three labels (APPLES, ORANGES, MIXED) are wrong. Drawing one fruit from one box of your choice, how do you correctly relabel all three?
puzzle.approach: Every label being wrong is a gift - start with the box whose wrong label rules out the most.
puzzle.answer: Draw from the box labelled MIXED. Its label is wrong, so it is pure. If you draw an apple it is the APPLES box; then ORANGES-labelled must be MIXED and APPLES-labelled must be ORANGES (mirror if you draw an orange). One draw suffices.

word_puzzle.title: For the Birds
word_puzzle.body: Sort 16 words into four groups of four: PAWN, SWIFT, WOLF, ROBIN, BISHOP, WREN, BOLT, JOKER, KNIGHT, SWALLOW, DOWN, PENGUIN, ROOK, FINCH, SCOFF, BANE.
word_puzzle.approach: Several words look like birds - but not all belong in the aviary.
word_puzzle.answer: Chess pieces: PAWN, KNIGHT, BISHOP, ROOK. Small birds: WREN, SWIFT, SWALLOW, FINCH. To eat/drink quickly: WOLF, BOLT, DOWN, SCOFF. Batman characters: ROBIN, JOKER, PENGUIN, BANE.
